task.name: forge triage: headless runs persist pending decisions; opt-in post-sprint trigger
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2230
---

## What

Headless triage. When `forge triage` runs without an operator present — post-sprint hook, cron, any non-interactive invocation — it stops at the reviewed-proposal stage and persists the whole package as a pending operator decision. `forge status` surfaces pending triage alongside pending HITL decisions; the operator picks it up later and ratification proceeds exactly as in the interactive flow.

Includes the opt-in trigger the epic promised: a config flag that runs the proposal stages automatically after a sprint completes.

## Why

Slice 5 of epic #1033, blocked by the ratification slice. The epic's pluggable-invocation goal — "TheForge supplies the workflow; the project wires it where it wants" — only works if a run with nobody at the keyboard is safe by construction. The safety property is inherited, not new: application already requires ratification, so a headless run that cannot ratify can only propose and persist.

## Acceptance criteria

- A headless invocation never blocks awaiting input and never applies any disposition; its product is a persisted pending-decision artifact containing the proposals, punt reviews, and evidence references.
- Pending triage decisions appear in `forge status` output alongside pending HITL decisions, with age and finding count, until resolved or explicitly discarded.
- Ratifying a persisted run applies exactly what was reviewed, under the same rules as interactive ratification — including the stale-entry rule: findings whose state changed since the proposal are surfaced and skipped, not blindly applied.
- The post-sprint trigger is opt-in configuration, default off; when enabled, a triage-stage failure is reported but never fails or blocks the sprint that triggered it.
- Repeated headless runs do not silently pile up: a new run that would supersede an unresolved pending decision says so and names the pending one, rather than burying it.

## Example

```
forge sprint ... --verbose
  ...sprint completes...
  triage: post-sprint pass proposed 3 dispositions (1 punt, concurred)
  triage: pending operator decision written — resolve with forge triage

forge status
  PENDING DECISIONS
    triage  2026-08-05  15 findings (2 flagged)  age 3h
```

## Non-goals

- No automated (operator-skipping) application in any confidence regime — explicitly deferred out of the epic, with its boundary recorded on the epic body.
- No scheduling/cron machinery of its own; external schedulers call the CLI.

handoff.summary: Headless `forge triage` now persists its reviewed proposal package as a durable pending operator decision. Extended `pending.py` with a kind discriminator plus triage-record helpers whose records deliberately carry no pid and no timeout_at, and made read_pending/cleanup_stale/sprint-status treat them as non-gates rather than sweeping them. Added coordinator/triage_headless_flow.py to own the collect→propose→review→persist orchestration and the one-unresolved-decision-per-project supersession refusal. cli/triage.py now picks its mode from stdin: any non-interactive invocation (with or without --report) runs the whole flow and persists, --no-audit is refused headless, --ratify refuses without a TTY before prompting or applying and accepts either the triage_run_id or the pending id, removing the pending artifact only when every outcome is terminal, and a new --discard drops one without applying anything. forge status renders triage entries with age and finding count next to HITL gates, and forge decide refuses them with the two commands that do resolve them. Added the opt-in sprint.post_sprint_triage config key (default false) and sprint/post_sprint_triage.py, called from run_sprint after the terminal result, catching every failure so a broken triage pass can never fail the sprint. The new config key enters configuration.recorded_values, so the audit record schema was bumped 36->37 with a documented no-op reader migration and a regenerated snapshot.

story_deviations: Plan step 6 described a sprint-owned helper doing the whole pass. The orchestration lives in coordinator/triage_headless_flow.py and the sprint helper delegates to it, so the CLI and the sprint share one implementation — required by the plan reviewer's P1 about bare non-interactive `forge triage`, and it keeps both call sites thin.

Added an audit record schema bump (36->37) with a no-op reader migration and regenerated snapshot, plus the version pin in tests/test_coord_policy_provenance_seam.py. Not in the plan, but unavoidable: configuration.recorded_values enumerates every resolved config key, so adding sprint.post_sprint_triage drifts the writer-side schema guard.

Added an autouse fixture to tests/test_cli_triage.py forcing stdin_is_interactive() True for the pre-existing tests. A pytest process has no TTY, so without it every existing test would silently exercise the new headless path rather than the interactive behaviour it was written to describe. No existing assertion was changed.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the cycle-1 P1: headless triage could publish a pending decision that a later `--ratify` would refuse, because ratify_triage_run resolves a run out of the audit substrate and the run's recording had failed. Added `_unratifiable_reason(summary, events)` in coordinator/triage_headless_flow.py, evaluated BEFORE the pending artifact is written, covering both independent failure modes: `summary.audit_error` set, and a run with findings whose recorded events reload empty (unreadable substrate / failed open). Either raises HeadlessTriageError naming the triage_run_id and finding count — the spend already happened, so the message must not read as a no-op — and no pending decision is written. An empty backlog records no events by construction and still persists normally. `_recorded_events` now documents that it deliberately does not interpret an empty reload; the caller decides. Both call sites already handled this correctly: the CLI prints the reason and exits 1, and the post-sprint helper catches it into a HEADLESS_FAILED outcome, so a recording failure still cannot fail the sprint. Also fixed the adjacent P2: pending.unresolved_triage_pending uses next(iter(...), None) instead of returning from the first loop iteration. Collateral audit found that the default `_recorded_events` stub in BOTH test files returned [] against a one-finding summary — every prior test was exercising the shape now rejected — so both helpers now stand in for the reload a real run would get, and the empty reload is covered as its own case rather than as an accident.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 persists only headless invocations using --report. In the actual src/theforge/cli/triage.py cmd_triage dispatch, an invocation with neither --ratify nor --report still calls _cmd_triage_report and returns after writing a backlog report. Therefore a cron or other ordinary non-interactive forge triage invocation would not run the proposal and punt-review stages or create the required pending decision.
  Suggestion: Extend the plan to change the headless no-mode dispatch path so it collects and writes the backlog report, runs the audited proposal/review flow, and persists the pending decision in one invocation, sharing that orchestration with the post-sprint helper. Add a CLI regression for plain forge triage with non-TTY stdin.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (pending.py assumes live process gates) is retired only in the two places the plan names. A third consumer exists outside the listed files: sprint/status_reader.py:745 _live_pending_records feeds _pending_entry_is_live (status_reader.py:604) and _pending_decision_display, which render pending files as story gates in sprint status. That filter requires an int pid that _is_pid_alive accepts, so a triage entry written *without* a pid is correctly invisible there — but if the implementation gives triage entries a pid for symmetry with HITL, they will surface as bogus live story gates with phase 'gate' and no remaining-time text.
  Suggestion: Make 'no pid on triage entries' an explicit invariant in Step 1 (and assert it in a Step 8 test), or filter on the kind discriminator in status_reader._pending_entry_is_live as well.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1's lookup surface (find by pending id or triage_run_id) has to coexist with pending.py's filename-as-key scheme: read_pending/resolve_pending/cleanup_pending all resolve .forge/pending/<run_id>.yaml, and read_pending deletes any file whose pid is missing or dead. A triage file dropped into that directory under any name is reachable by forge decide <name>/read_pending and would be unlinked on first read.
  Suggestion: Pick the triage filename scheme deliberately (e.g. a triage-<triage_run_id>.yaml prefix) and short-circuit the kind check in read_pending *before* the pid-liveness cleanup, not after.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 1 (undefined supersession key) is carried but conservatively bounded: the plan picks one-unresolved-triage-pending-per-project. That satisfies the AC, but the refusal path in Step 6 (post-sprint) must not be silent — a sprint that skips triage because of an existing pending decision needs to say so in sprint output, not only in a return value.
  Suggestion: Have the Step 9 supersession test assert on the operator-visible sprint log line, not just that no proposal pass started.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 3 (dependency on the issue-2230 ratification substrate) does not apply on this branch — ratify_triage_run, _stale_reason, _upsert_application, and STATUS_STALE are all present in coordinator/triage_ratification_flow.py, and cli/triage.py already exposes --ratify. The 'stop rather than reimplement' mitigation is moot.
  Suggestion: No action; recorded so the risk is not dropped silently.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] When testing headless/non-interactive behavior, relying solely on sys.stdin.isatty() can be fragile in test environments or CI runners where stdin may be mocked.

finding_registry.description: When the proposal stage reports an audit write failure, headless triage still writes a pending decision and advertises it as ratifiable, but later ratification cannot find the recorded proposal run in the audit substrate.
The function unresolved_triage_pending retrieves the oldest pending decision by returning on the first iteration of an explicit loop.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
